newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hoechst to sell Australia plastic unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hoechst to sell Australia plastic unit.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG has agreed to sell its Australian plastics business to Kemcor Australia Ltd, a joint venture between oil majors Mobil Corp and Exxon Corp, the parties said on Wednesday.
The sale price was not disclosed. The sale is subject to due diligence, Hoechst and Kemcor said.
Under the deal, sealed in a memorandum of understanding, Hoechst's Australian plastics operation at the Altona refinery in Melbourne would be sold to Kemcor, the parties said.
Kemcor, which makes the feedstock consumed in all of the plastics resin-making at Altona, said the purchase would double its plastics production capacity to 260,000 tonnes per annum.
The move would make Kemcor the biggest producer of polyethylene and polypropylene plastics in Australia, it added.
Hoechst Australia's managing director, Jens Mohr, said the sale did not include the company's non-polymer businesses.

He said the divestment supported the Hoechst group's strategy to focus on core businesses and reflected the need for domestic plastics manufacturers to become bigger to withstand falling tariff barriers on plastics imports.

"The recent world-wide restructuring of the international Hoechst group has seen it focus on core businesses in the three main areas of pharmaceuticals, agrichemicals and industrial chemicals," Mohr said in a statement.
"Our aim is to be one of the worldwide leaders in each of our main areas of activity and the proposed divestment to Kemcor supports this strategy."

But he said the Hoechst group would remain in the plastics business, especially in Europe where it recently announced plans to form a polypropylene joint venture with another German chemicals group, BASF
Kemcor spokeswoman Dahle Suggett told Reuters the sale was worth tens of millions of dollars but declined to name the sum.

Polyethylene is used to make products for many sectors of the economy, including construction and packaging industries. Polypropylene is commonly made into plastic mouldings for the car and furniture industries.
"The whole deal is about greater competitiveness for the Australian industry," Kemcor's Suggett said, adding that falling tariffs were exposing the local industry to more Asian imports.
High-density polyethylene imports from such countries as Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea and Taiwan had captured 23 percent of the Australian market, she said.
"It (the purchase) is a step to increase our scale of production and get our unit costs down and set the platform for further growth," Suggett said.
